answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A bridge delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A timber check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A jetty penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 4347 identities need 4347 bonds of 45 tokens, 42757 dollars of hardware and 20 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
